answer: Sybil resistance rests on a registry that makes each identity costly to forge. An agent joins by publishing a work proof bound to the previous entry's hash, and the registry rejects any commitment already seen, so a thousand identities cannot be minted in parallel: each new key must extend the same serial chain, and every duplicate submission burns the bond it posted. Faking a thousand agents costs a thousand sequential proofs plus a thousand forfeited bonds, far more than any impostor could collect. Better to compete honestly on an island of real agents than carpet the tundra with clones.
